findings.evidence: "Similarly, the IT asset group tracks the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month."
findings.fix: Identify a single owner for the equipment catalog and specify one update cadence - either IT asset group tracks it monthly, or finance liaison publishes it at fiscal year start, not both.
findings.violation: Later in the document, the equipment catalog is attributed to the finance liaison ("publishes the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year") and the benefits team ("reviews the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year"), creating confusion about who actually maintains it.

findings.evidence: "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: Replace with explicit language: "Employees are re-eligible upon return from approved leave. The 90-day continuous service period begins anew on their first day back."
findings.violation: "Clock" is ambiguous - it's unclear whether the 90-day continuous service requirement resets or whether the employee is immediately re-eligible with prior service counted toward the requirement.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Replace with: "Complete the request in this order: confirm eligibility, upload the receipt, review the confirmation summary, and submit the final request."
findings.location: How to Apply section, "Request Steps" line
findings.violation: This sentence is incomplete and identifies only two steps when the process described earlier includes reviewing a confirmation summary before submission.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Replace with: "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition. The benefits team may request a photo verification annually."
findings.violation: Shifts to second person ("You" and "we") while the rest of the document uses third person, creating tone inconsistency.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.fix: Clarify: "Employees may claim one device per equipment category per benefit year."
findings.violation: The time frame is missing - "one device per category per employee" does not specify whether this limit applies per benefit year, per calendar year, or lifetime.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review."
findings.fix: Define the term once and use third person: "Each claimed piece of equipment is recorded as a stipend item. Finance reconciles all stipend items against the request log monthly. Payroll processes reimbursement after that reconciliation."
findings.violation: "Stipend item" is used three times without definition, and the paragraph shifts to second person with "you" while the rest of the policy uses third person.

findings.evidence: "However, an incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives."
findings.fix: Replace with: "An incomplete request pauses the timeline until the employee submits the missing documentation. The employee receives an automatic reminder after three days."
findings.violation: "Missing item" is ambiguous - it could refer to missing documentation or the equipment itself not yet being shipped.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests. Additionally, employees must retain receipts for one year after the purchase date."
findings.fix: Clarify: "Employees may submit a photo of the receipt with their request. However, employees must retain the original receipt for one year to support audit reconciliation."
findings.violation: These statements appear contradictory - if a photo satisfies the submission requirement, the purpose and scope of the one-year physical retention requirement is unclear.

findings.evidence: "The finance office deposits the amount within one pay cycle" (Reimbursement Amounts) vs. "Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review" (Terminology Notes)
findings.fix: Consolidate: "After approval, finance routes the reimbursement to payroll, which deposits the amount within one pay cycle."
findings.location: Reimbursement Amounts section vs. Terminology Notes
findings.violation: Two different departments are named as handling the actual payment, creating confusion about whether finance or payroll processes the reimbursement.

findings.evidence: "The manager reviews the request within two business days" (Approval Timeline) vs. "The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out" (Review Responsibility)
findings.fix: Combine into a single approval section: "The manager conducts the initial review within two business days. Any request exceeding $200 is then reviewed by finance before reimbursement, and finance flags any requests repeating within the same quarter."
findings.location: Approval Timeline section vs. Review Responsibility section
findings.violation: Two separate review processes are described without clarifying their sequence or how they interact - it's unclear whether both occur or if the finance review is conditional.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Replace with: "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition. The benefits team may request a dated photo of equipment once annually to verify condition."
findings.violation: "Brief photo check" is undefined - the scope, format, and what is being verified is not specified.
